judge_assessment.explanation: Every judge claim holds against the artifacts. I re-solved all eight stories and confirmed which quantity each asks for: 18 stickers into 3 bags asks group SIZE (6), 20 stickers at 5 per bag asks group COUNT (4), 24 crackers at 4 per plate asks count (6), 35 seeds in 5 pots asks size (7), the missing-factor equation g x 8 = 48 asks count (6), 40 markers at 8 each asks count (5), Ben's 36 shells in 4 rows asks size (9), and problem 8(b)'s 30 pencils at 6 per cup asks count (5) — matching verify.json entry for entry. The judge's specific check on the open comparison is also right: 30 pencils at 6 per cup gives 5 cups while 30 pencils in 5 cups gives 6 per cup, which is exactly the symmetry problem 8(a) asks the child to articulate, and the judge's manual_items_reviewed: 1 matches the single {"id": 8, "type": "manual"} entry. This case is the run's best example of the two canonical failures NOT happening: problem 8 is split into a manual entry for the explanation and a separate eval entry for the computation, and the build correctly exits with a manual flag (machine_observation gate_chain_manual_flags: true). One thing the judge did not examine, which I raise as a bounded finding rather than a disagreement: problem 6 prints a scaffold question ('First check Rio's answer by multiplying: 8 groups with 8 markers in each group. Is that total bigger or smaller than 40?') and problem 3 prints an identification question ('Ravi wrote back a number the story already told him. Which one was it?') whose answers — 'bigger, because 8 x 8 = 64' and '4' — have determinate values that verify.json never records.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8 is the template the rest of the run should copy: verify.json carries TWO entries under id 8, a {"type": "manual"} entry whose desc states the full-credit criteria ('says that the words after the number decide it ... and that the total is always the number being shared') and a separate {"type": "eval", "expr": "t/s", "expected": 5} for part (b). The answer key mirrors the split, printing '(a) Open response — flagged for manual review' with a model answer and a 'What a full-credit answer must contain' line, then a fully worked (b).

Every declared trap is the GIVEN number itself — expr 'g' or expr 's', never an arithmetic slip — which makes the trap the misconception rather than a generic wrong answer. The numbers were chosen so the two never coincide, and final_response.md states the reasoning: 'a story with 6 groups of 6 would be blind to the error it is meant to catch.'

Problem 7 puts Jen's story (36 shells, 4 in each row) beside Ben's (36 shells, 4 rows) so the SAME two numbers appear with swapped jobs, and the trap is declared as 'the other child's story'. This is the sharpest single item on the sheet for the stated focus.

final_response.md is candid about a real repository gap rather than papering over it: references/standards-map.md has no row for 3.OA.A.2 or 3.OA.A.4, the two codes closest to this focus, so the problems are tagged with the row that genuinely covers them instead of an invented code.

root_causes.description: A problem may print a scaffold sub-question with a determinate answer alongside its main answer, and no gate compares the number of printed response slots with the number of verify entries covering that id. The two extra slots here are teaching scaffolds rather than the graded answer, so the impact is bounded, but the mechanism is the same one that leaves whole answers unchecked elsewhere in the run.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 6 prints two questions: 'Is that total bigger or smaller than 40?' and 'Then write how many groups really get markers.' verify.json id 6 has one entry, {"type": "eval", "expr": "t/s", "at": {"t": 40, "s": 8}, "expected": 5}. The comparison 8 x 8 = 64 > 40 is machine-checkable (a compare entry) and is not recorded.

worksheet.pdf problem 3 prints 'Which one was it? Then write how many plates there really are.' verify.json id 3 has one entry, expected 6; the identification answer 4 appears only as a trap value, which prints under 'Common wrong answers' rather than as a checked response.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '3. 6' and '6. 5' — one value each for problems that ask two things.

improvements.title: Fail the build when a problem prints more answer blanks than its verify entries cover
improvements.proposed_change: In tests/check_answer_line.py (which already takes both the worksheet .tex and verify.json and runs as build.sh gate 10), count the answer-location macros per problem region and compare against the number of verify entries for that id carrying an 'expected' value or "type": "manual". Exit 1 on an undercount, naming the problem and the two remedies (add the entry, or fold the scaffold into the single graded line). For this case the fix is small and content-preserving: add a {"type": "compare", "values": ["8*8", "40"], "order": "relation", "expected": ">"} entry under id 6 so the 'bigger or smaller' step the problem explicitly asks for is proved, and either record the identification answer under id 3 or reword the stem so the one graded answer is the plate count.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/fixtures/slot_undercount/ with a worksheet whose problem 1 prints two \ansblank ('Is 8 x 8 bigger or smaller than 40?~\ansblank How many groups really get markers?~\ansblank') against a verify.json with a single id-1 entry (expected 5). Assert check_answer_line.py exits 1 with '2 printed answer slots, 1 covered'; add the second entry and assert exit 0.
improvements.expected_impact: Bounded here — this sheet's graded answers are all verified and the key explains both scaffold steps in prose, so no learner is misled today. The value is uniformity: the same gate that catches curr-096's six unverified bar readings also catches this, so authors get one rule rather than a judgement call about which sub-questions 'count'.
improvements.risk: Scaffold blanks are a deliberate and good design on early-elementary sheets (they slow the child down before the aggregate). A gate that forces a JSON entry for every one of them could push authors to delete the scaffolds instead, which would make the sheets worse. The failure message must offer 'declare the value' first and 'merge the lines' second, and the SKILL.md wording should say plainly that scaffolds are welcome as long as their answers are checked.

case_summary: The strongest case in this batch and the one the rest of the run should be measured against. All eight quotients are correct and, more to the point, every problem asks for the quantity the focus is about: four items ask for group size and four for group count, with the given number always available as the wrong answer. Every trap expression is the given number itself (g or s), machine-proved distinguishable, so a wrong answer diagnoses the misconception instead of merely being wrong. Problem 7's twin stories share the same two numbers with swapped jobs. Most importantly, problem 8 does what 36 other cases in this run did not: its explanation part is declared {"type": "manual"} with an explicit full-credit rubric, its computation part is a separate machine check, the build exits 2 with exactly one manual item, and final_response.md says so. The only gap I found is bounded — problem 6's 'is that total bigger or smaller than 40?' and problem 3's 'which number did Ravi write back?' print response slots whose answers verify.json never records, though the answer key works both through in prose. I agree with the judge's ACCEPT and with all eight dimension scores.
